messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Detecting a run with numerical error
parts:
It's hard to diagnose problems like this without the model.
You don't want to just throw things away and try again---those
messages are signaling potential problems in the fit.

We recommend reducing adapt_delta further and if that still doesn't
solve the problem, then we recommend reparameterizing.

It helps Stan's adaptation immensely if parameter posteriors
are roughly unit scale (zero mean and unit variance).

And we always recommend running multiple chains to diagnose
potential convergence problems.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Detecting a run with numerical error
parts:
> On Feb 14, 2017, at 6:35 PM, Leon Peshkin <pes...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> But you can see in my command line that adapt_delta is already .95 ... not much room for increase there.

If you think of it as how close to 1 you get, you have orders of
magnitude room for increase.
> Also if I run multiple chains usually only one has this issue.

What you need to validate is that you get the right coverage for
simulated data. Sometimes the resulting bias in the sampler from
not being able to get into a region due to divergences will be
minor, but it always signals arithmetic problems in the Hamiltonian
in some part of the posterior the sampler is visiting.

> I took your suggestion of re-parametrizing to heart, yet I'd like to feel somewhat in control of the sampling,
> isn't there a way for me to see in returned results that there was this issue in addition to it just being spit
> as the output.

Yes, but I'm not sure how to pull it out of RStan, because it's
not stored the same way as other per-draw information.

You can also visualize it in ShinyStan.
> by the way there is a typo "occurs" ....

Sorry, but I'm missing the context --- where's the typo?

- Bob
